children: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has settled adjudication proceedings against five Adani group companies for a combined ₹1.51 crore over alleged disclosure and compliance lapses, including a related-party transaction (RPT) disclosure issue and audit reports signed by firms without valid peer-review certificates.

Adani Enterprises paid ₹76.05 lakh, Adani Green Energy ₹45.50 lakh, while Adani Total Gas, AWL Agri Business and Adani Energy Solutions paid ₹9.75 lakh each.
The five companies settled the proceedings without admitting or denying the findings of fact and conclusions of law.
IRB Infrastructure to monetise non-core assets
The Board of Directors of IRB Infrastructure has given in-principle approval and authorised the Company to monetise its non-core assets, by way of:
phased development of land parcels of around 350 acres out of total 1,100 acres owned by Aryan Infrastructure Developers Limited at Taje and Pimpaloli, Pune;
and redevelopment and rehabilitation of part of land parcels of ~ 3,500 sq. mts. owned by Ideal Road Builders Private Limited at Chandivali, Mumbai.
RailTel receives ₹14.09-crore work order
RailTel Corporation of India Ltd has received the Work Order from Uttar Pradesh University of Medical Sciences.
The order value, as per the Work Order, is Rs 14.09 crore (including Tax).
Persistent Systems crosses Nagarro takeover threshold
Persistent Systems has successfully crossed the minimum threshold in its public takeover bid for German digital engineering firm Nagarro SE, accumulating an 83.25% stake.
Under German takeover laws, remaining minority shareholders can tender their holdings during an additional window from September 23 to October 6, 2026, at the initial cash price of EUR 81 per share.
The IT firm intends to take Nagarro SE private by initiating delisting procedures from the Frankfurt Stock Exchange’s Prime Standard.
Aashish Agarwal joins 360 ONE WAM as CEO

Aashish Agarwal, former Managing Director and India Head of Jefferies, has joined 360 ONE WAM Group as Chief Executive Officer, marking a significant leadership transition at one of India’s largest wealth and asset managers.

Under the new structure, Karan Bhagat, currently Managing Director & CEO, will become Vice-Chairman while continuing as Managing Director, focusing on strategy, capital allocation and key client relationships.
Yatin Shah will continue to lead the wealth management business.
360 ONE manages over ₹7.8 lakh crore in assets and serves more than 8,900 families, corporates and institutions.
Fredun Pharma acquires 26% in Goodman Vetcare
Fredun Pharmaceuticals Limited has acquired a 26 per cent stake in Goodman Vetcare Private Limited for an undisclosed sum.
This is Fredun Pharma’s second acquisition in the animal health and veterinary retail and pet-care market, in less than two weeks.
The acquisition gives Fredun Pharma a foothold into Goodman’s established retail network.
Earlier this month, it had acquired USV’s pet-wellness brand Furlicks, for an undisclosed sum.
Veranda Learning promoters pledge shares

Veranda Learning Solutions said in an exchange filing on Tuesday that its Promoters — Kalpathi S Aghoram, Kalpathi S Ganesh and Kalpathi S Suresh — have executed an unattested pledge agreement with Authum Investment & Infrastructure Ltd to create a pledge over equity shares of Veranda Learning held by them.
The agreement covers an ₹111 crore loan that the promoters availed in their personal capacity from the lender.
